explanation: The M230L mutation reduces nevirapine binding through a subtle loss of favorable van der Waals interactions at the NNRTI-binding pocket wall. Methionine's longer, flexible sulfur-containing side chain provides superior shape complementarity and polarizable contacts with nevirapine's aromatic core at the 2.8 Å binding interface, whereas leucine's shorter branched aliphatic chain cannot achieve the same contact surface area despite the minimal 3.8 Å³ volume decrease. This modest energetic penalty (~0.01 kcal/mol) accumulates because methionine's unique ability to optimize van der Waals packing in the primer grip region is lost when replaced with the more constrained leucine scaffold.
